messages:
Elena: Quick heads-up — we just rolled BurstOptimizer to canary for runtime (prefetch + dynamic microburst packing). Early numbers: p50 latency down 18%, p95 down 12%, token cost down 22% on typical chat workloads. Rolling to beta tomorrow.

Mike: Awesome. Any impact on Dedicated customers or SLA risk? :eyes:

Elena: Dedicated pools unaffected by default; rollout only hits hosted API and canaries. For Dedicated we have a config flag `redwood.runtime.enable_burst_optimizer=false` until we opt in. No SLA regressions seen in canary.

Jess: Where can we see the benchmark artifacts and perf dashboards?

Elena: Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/burstoptimizer
Bench artifacts in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/benchmarks/burst-optimizer/results
Snippet to enable for a test node:
```
# enable on a single node
rctl set runtime.burst_optimizer.enabled=true --node=node-12-canary
```

infra-bot: Canary summary (12 nodes): p50 18% ↓, p95 12% ↓, token-cost 22% ↓. No OOMs, CPU stable. Logs: /logs/burst-optimizer/canary-1765554321

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started by Elena at 1765554420

deploy-bot: canary-deploy succeeded at 1765554870

Sam: Did we run the eval set for instruction-following regressions? We hit a weird sample last time with aggressive batching.

Elena: Good call — ran eval suite v2026-03-22 against the canary, regression rate <0.2% and within threshold. Full eval report attached in GH link above.

Mike: Cool. What's the rollout plan?

Elena: Rollout timeline:
- Tomorrow 09:00 UTC: expand canary to 60 nodes
- +48h: incremental 25% traffic by sharding policy
- +96h: full rollout if no regressions
Rollback policy: automatic fallback to previous runtime on p95 latency >10% of baseline or error spike >1.5%.

Jess: I'll add a dashboard tile for cost per 1k tokens. Thanks!

Elena: Thanks all — shout if you see anything weird. :rocket:
